theme: El camino a Belén — la ciudad y el pueblo, las direcciones, el transporte, ir a + lugar, las órdenes familiares
storyThread: El camino a Belén (Lucas 2:1-7): el empadronamiento, el viaje de Nazaret a Belén, y el pesebre. L1 = el pueblo y sus lugares (re-pass de ciudad/calle/tienda/muro/camino); L2 = las direcciones; L3 = el transporte y el viaje (el paradigma de ir); L4 = las órdenes del camino y la llegada al pesebre.
grammarTargets: ir a + lugar: voy / va / van (+ vamos re-pass de a0-verbs). VAS IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — near-form budget, deferred to A1-U8 (two-verb structures / invitations); same treatment as C7's tenemos exclusion

a + el → al: the contraction is bound as its own id; bare a is bound too (closes the unbound spoken forms «va a la ciudad» a1-u01, «Vamos al pueblo»/«Al norte» a0-u05). a and al NEVER share an option set
familiar (tú) affirmative imperatives: ve, ven, dobla, sigue, cruza, espera + re-pass mira (a0-verbs). No negative commands (no + infinitive is A1-U8/B1-U2), no vosotros forms
present tense ONLY — pretérito is A1-U7. The scripture passage is past tense and is exempt per the standing scripture ruling
directions as adverbs: a la derecha, a la izquierda, todo recto, arriba, abajo — the phrase lives in say/sign, the tile is the bare form (formIdRule)
place nouns keep their articles (el pueblo, la plaza, al mercado); los/las already shipped in a1-u01 — no new article teaching
waveNotes: l1 (8) = the town: 5 byte-identical re-passes (ciudad a0-signs-regions, calle a1-u01, tienda a0-u03, muro a1-u01, camino a0-u05) + pueblo/plaza/mercado new. NO pue- near pair inside l1 (puerta deliberately NOT re-passed here — re-served in a0-u03 + a1-u01 + a1-u02; puente sits in l2, away from pueblo). l2 (10) = directions + the bridge landmark: 6 new (derecha, izquierda, recto, arriba, abajo, puente) + 4 re-passes (cerca/lejos a1-u02, norte/sur a0-u05); contrast pairs sit together on purpose (derecha/izquierda, arriba/abajo, norte/sur, cerca/lejos) — documented exception. l3 (8) = transport + the ir paradigm: burro/camello/carro/viaje new, vamos re-pass, voy/va/van new. The whole ir paradigm is in ONE wave (a1-u02's tener-paradigm precedent) with the minimal pairs va/van separated inside it. l4 (10) = the orders of the road + the arrival: ve/ven/dobla/sigue/cruza/espera/a/al/pesebre new + mira re-pass; a and al are here because the commands carry them («Ve a la plaza.», «Ve al pueblo.»). Largest wave = 10 — under the 12-per-page threshold (DEFECTS #18), no pagination. Wave 5 = adaptive replay from progress.misses (unchanged convention — matches a1-u01/a1-u02).

scripture.verse: Y ACONTECIÓ en aquellos días que salió edicto de parte de Augusto César, que toda la tierra fuese empadronada. Este empadronamiento primero fué hecho siendo Cirenio gobernador de la Siria. E iban todos para ser empadronados, cada uno á su ciudad. Y subió José de Galilea, de la ciudad de Nazaret, á Judea, á la ciudad de David, que se llama Bethlehem, por cuanto era de la casa y familia de David; Para ser empadronado con María su mujer, desposada con él, la cual estaba en cinta. Y aconteció que estando ellos allí, se cumplieron los días en que ella había de parir. Y parió á su hijo primogénito, y le envolvió en pañales, y acostóle en un pesebre, porque no había lugar para ellos en el mesón.

qna.charset: ASCII + á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡ in rendered fields; « » only in scripture.say (spoken-only). Proper nouns Belén, María, José, Jesús appear in say text and are never tiles (a1-u02 Obed-Edom rule).
qna.nearFormRule: Never in the same word-round option set: cómo/como, vivo/vive, cree/crece/creó, por qué/porque, muro/pared, mi/mío, tu/tú, tiene/tienen, tienes/tiene, en/entre, nuevo/nuestro (inherited from a1-u02 and still binding). NEW in this pack: va/van (final -n only — the tiene/tienen family), ve/ven, ve/va, a/al, pueblo/puerta/puente (pue- cluster), puente/puerta, plaza/plato/planta (pla- cluster), barro/burro, barro/carro, viaje/viejo, camello/camino, cruza/crece/cree, espera/escribe, cama/casa. DOCUMENTED EXCEPTIONS (deliberate, kept): (1) the taught contrast pairs sit TOGETHER in one set — derecha/izquierda, arriba/abajo, norte/sur, cerca/lejos — because the pair IS the teaching point (a1-u02's cerca/lejos and a0-u05's norte/sur precedent); (2) ir-paradigm members voy/va/van/vamos MAY share a set — only the minimal pairs are separated (a1-u02 allowed the tener family on exactly this logic); (3) a1-u02's exceptions (hay/está/tengo, mi/tu/su, cuántos/cuándo) remain documented exceptions but none of those ids co-occur in this pack's sets. Phantom decoys: none — every option string is a bound pool id.
qna.pagination: largest wave l2/l4 = 10 ids, l1/l3 = 8 — all under the 12-per-page threshold (DEFECTS #18). No split required.
qna.englishLevel: A1 — caption gloss optional, fades at immersion ≥1
qna.duplicateCheck: 25 new ids, 0 collisions against the 250-id taught pool (unit-01 53 incl. te llamas + a0-packs 49 + a0-verbs 30 + a0-u02 45 + a0-u06 28 + a1-u01 22 + a1-u02 23 = 250). 11 re-passes are byte-identical re-serves with new:false + poolSource, never re-introduced as new. Pool after this pack = 275.
qna.optionsBoundToIds: Every option string is a bound pool id (250 existing + this pack's 25). Decoys drawn from the same wave where possible (burro/camello/carro, dobla/sigue/cruza) and from a1-u02's function words for a/al (de, en). No phantom decoys (DEFECTS #14).
qna.grammar: A1 register per THEOLOGY-guide §3.1: present tense only, NO pretérito (A1-U7 owns it), NO subjunctive, affirmative familiar imperatives only (ve/ven/dobla/sigue/cruza/espera/mira). Every say is one idea and the target word is repeated in caption + sign. Scripture exempt from the tense rule (standing ruling).
qna.csa: Owner plain-truth directive applied: no sanitizing rules apply. Content guard held voluntarily: NOTHING in this pack invents nativity detail beyond Lucas 2:1-7 — no donkey for María, no animals at the manger, no innkeeper, no «no hay lugar» dramatization. The donkey/camel/cart are generic transport vocabulary in their own sentences. The pesebre is stated plainly («Jesús está en el pesebre»), which is what the text says. INT-1 holds — no doctrine-assent gate anywhere.
qna.formIdRule: ids are the exact form the learner hears and the string on the tile. Directions are BARE (derecha, izquierda, recto, arriba, abajo) while the phrase «a la derecha» / «todo recto» lives in say/sign — the tile stays a word (a0-u06 question-word precedent). ir forms are finite forms (voy/va/van), not the infinitive (a0-verbs formIdRule). al is the contraction, not a + el split.
